newsitem.title: GREECE: WORLD BANK PUSHES AHEAD WITH DEBT RELIEF PLAN.
newsitem.headline: WORLD BANK PUSHES AHEAD WITH DEBT RELIEF PLAN.

text.p: Representatives of the major industrialised countries and multilateral institutions agreed on Thursday to the speedy implementation of the heavily indebted poor countries' (HIPC) debt initiative, the Paris-based World Bank office said in a statement.

"This meeting has provided an important opportunity to reach a shared understanding of how all the parties involved are going to proceed quickly, in a collaborative manner, to implement this joint effort and ensure that countries gain access to the benefits of the initiative as soon as possible," Sven Sandstrom, managing director at World Bank was quoted as saying.
The HIPC debt initiative was proposed by the World Bank and IMF and was agreed by governments from all over the world in Washington at the end September, it said.

The HIPC initiative aims to enable poor countries with good policy performance to sustain development and reduce poverty by providing relief on debts owed to participating multilateral development institutions, it said.

The HIPC initiative includes the new HIPC Trust Fund which was formally set up by the World Bank's board of executive directors on November 7 and will be administered by the World Bank's International Development Association (IDA), it said.
The IDA is the World Bank's lending arm for concessional loans to the poorest countries.
"The World Bank has set aside $500 million as an initial contribution to the Trust Fund to meet its share of debt relief," said the statement.
